domain_label: Instructional Media & 3D Flashcard Producer — Multimedia Learning Science
purpose: The pedagogical science that decides WHAT card media to produce and HOW: Mayer's cognitive theory of multimedia learning (dual-channel, limited-capacity, active processing) and its design principles (multimedia, coherence, signaling, redundancy, modality, spatial and temporal contiguity, segmenting/pretraining), the anatomy-education evidence on 3D-vs-2D for spatial content moderated by learner spatial ability, and the cost-ledger decision rule for when a diagram or 3D model earns its cognitive cost versus when it is decoration — kept honest by tagging every load-bearing claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN and tracing vendor pipeline facts to EXTERNAL_RECON.
assumptions: no observed dataset or learner eye-tracking is supplied; all scores are heuristic priors and every effect-size claim is a literature-synthesis ESTIMATE to source-verify, not a measurement on this app's learner

Mayer's CTML and its principles are domain science this author is confident of but has NOT re-derived from the primary sources in this build, so they are tagged [ESTIMATE — to source-verify] rather than [FACT]

this KB owns the WHY (learning-science decision to produce/skip/format media); the image->Tripo->GLB->model-viewer PRODUCTION pipeline mechanics and the Codex MCP image generator are neighboring media-KB slices referenced here only at the decision boundary
image occlusion CONSUMES images inside the contenteng specialist; this KB governs the pedagogy of PRODUCING those images and 3D models, not the occlusion card lifecycle
the single-user study app serves an INBDE/TOEFL learner, so 'anatomy' means dental/head-and-neck spatial content and the media budget (generation credits, screen, attention) is scarce
exclusions: the Tripo API call surface, GLB conversion parameters, and <model-viewer> HTML wiring beyond naming them as the gated downstream pipeline (neighboring media KB / extint)
the Codex-MCP-via-extint image-generation call mechanics and prompt engineering beyond stating that a produce-decision hands off to it
the image-occlusion card object model, occlusion-mask editing and scheduling (owned by contenteng) beyond emitting the pedagogical media spec it consumes
the knowledge-graph / concept-tag data model and card-authoring pipeline (contenteng/kgraph) beyond taking a concept and its spatial character as input
colour-encoding, chart, and graph-view rendering science (viz specialist) beyond the signaling/contiguity principles that touch diagram legibility

competency_questions.question: What are the three assumptions of Mayer's cognitive theory of multimedia learning and why do they bound every media-production decision?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names the dual-channel (visual/pictorial and auditory/verbal), limited-capacity, and active/generative-processing assumptions, ties them to Paivio dual-coding and Baddeley working memory, and states that limited capacity is why extraneous media harms, tagged ESTIMATE to source-verify

competency_questions.question: What are the three kinds of cognitive load / processing demand, and which one is the media producer's lever?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: defines intrinsic (essential), extraneous (incidental), and germane (generative) load per Sweller/Mayer, states intrinsic is set by content and germane is desired, and identifies extraneous load from poor media design as the thing to minimise

competency_questions.question: What is the multimedia principle and does it justify adding an image to every card?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states people learn better from words plus pictures than words alone, but that the benefit is conditional on the picture being relevant and well-designed, so it justifies RELEVANT media not decoration on every card

competency_questions.question: What do the coherence principle and the seductive-details effect say to exclude, and why?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that excluding extraneous words, sounds and images improves learning, names the seductive-details effect where interesting-but-irrelevant content harms, and grounds both in limited capacity

competency_questions.question: What is the signaling principle and how does it apply to a produced diagram or occlusion image?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that cues (arrows, highlights, labels, bolding) directing attention to essential material improve learning without adding content, and applies it to guiding the eye to the structure a card tests

competency_questions.question: What do the redundancy and modality principles say about narration, on-screen text and graphics together?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that graphics plus narration usually beats graphics plus narration plus identical on-screen text (redundancy), and that narration can beat on-screen text for transient animations (modality), both explained by channel overload, with the exceptions noted

competency_questions.question: What do spatial and temporal contiguity require when placing labels on an anatomical diagram?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that corresponding words and pictures should be placed near each other on the page (spatial) and presented at the same time (temporal), so labels sit adjacent to their referents rather than in a distant legend

competency_questions.question: How do segmenting and pretraining manage essential processing for a complex anatomical structure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that breaking a complex model into learner-paced segments and pre-teaching the names/parts before the full presentation reduce essential-load overload, and maps this to layered/labelled reveal of a structure

competency_questions.question: Does a 3D model beat a 2D image for spatial anatomy, and how does learner spatial ability moderate the answer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the evidence is mixed and content-dependent, that 3D helps most for inherently spatial structural relations, and that spatial ability moderates it (ability-as-compensator vs enhancer/expertise-reversal), tagged ESTIMATE to source-verify

competency_questions.question: When does interactivity/stereopsis help a 3D model and when does manipulating it overload the learner?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that active rotation and depth cues can aid spatial understanding but that the manipulation itself adds extraneous load, so unguided free 3D can harm, and that instructional guidance/fading is needed

competency_questions.question: How do you decide whether a diagram or 3D model earns its cognitive cost versus being decoration?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives the cost-ledger comparison (production cost plus processing load versus learning payoff), the rule that a visual earns its cost only when the content is inherently spatial/structural and the visual carries information words cannot, and the default-to-skip for arbitrary/verbal facts

competency_questions.question: What is the pedagogical spec for a produced image-occlusion diagram that contenteng will consume?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that occlusion images must apply signaling and spatial contiguity, keep one testable structure per occludable region, avoid seductive detail, and label referents adjacently so each masked region is an unambiguous retrieval target

competency_questions.question: When should the image->Tripo->GLB->model-viewer 3D pipeline be invoked rather than a 2D image?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives the gate (inherently 3D spatial relations that 2D cannot convey AND the model can be guided/segmented AND the cost is justified), names GLB output rendered by <model-viewer> per EXTERNAL_RECON, and defaults to 2D otherwise

competency_questions.question: What is the overall produce/skip/format media verdict for a given card and concept?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: composes the decision policy: skip media for verbal/arbitrary facts, 2D signaled diagram for spatial-on-a-plane content, gated 3D for inherently volumetric structural content, always applying coherence/signaling/contiguity and defaulting to the cheaper honest option

glossary.definition: Mayer's theory that meaningful multimedia learning rests on three assumptions — dual channels (separate visual/pictorial and auditory/verbal processing), limited capacity per channel, and active processing (selecting, organising, integrating) — from which the design principles are derived [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

Sweller's three demands on limited working memory: intrinsic (essential, set by the content's complexity and element interactivity), extraneous (incidental, imposed by poor presentation design), and germane (generative, the desirable effort of building a schema); good media minimises extraneous load to free capacity for germane processing [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

People learn better from words and pictures together than from words alone, provided the picture is relevant and well-designed; the base justification for producing card media at all, but conditional not universal [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

Learning improves when extraneous words, sounds and images are excluded; the seductive-details effect is the specific harm of interesting-but-irrelevant additions that compete for limited capacity and disrupt schema building [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

Adding cues that highlight the organisation of, or direct attention to, essential material (arrows, colour highlight, labels, bolding) improves learning without adding new content [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

Redundancy: graphics plus narration usually beats graphics plus narration plus identical on-screen text; modality: for transient animation, spoken words can beat on-screen text because they use the auditory channel and free the visual channel for the graphic — both explained by avoiding within-channel overload, each with boundary exceptions [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

Corresponding words and pictures should be placed near each other in space (labels adjacent to referents, not in a distant legend) and presented at the same time, so the learner does not spend capacity holding one while searching for the other [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

The anatomy-education finding that interactive/stereoscopic 3D models help learning of inherently spatial structural relations for some learners but not uniformly; effects are moderated by learner spatial ability and by whether the manipulation is guided, and results are mixed across studies [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

Learner visuospatial ability changes 3D's benefit: under the ability-as-compensator view rich external 3D helps low-spatial learners most, while under enhancer/expertise-reversal views added visual richness can overload high-ability or advanced learners for whom a static 2D image suffices [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

The house decision rule: a produced visual is justified only when its total cost (generation credits, screen real estate, and the extraneous load of processing it) is outweighed by a learning payoff that words alone cannot deliver — which happens when the content is inherently spatial/structural; otherwise the visual is decoration and is skipped.

GLB is the binary glTF 3D asset format Tripo emits (model.glb, pbr_model); Google's <model-viewer> web component renders glTF/GLB in-browser via a three.js loader, so a produced 3D anatomy asset can be shown with one HTML tag [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7].

nodes.definition: Frame the whole specialist slice: card media (a diagram, an occlusion image, a 3D anatomy model) is an instructional intervention that must be judged by whether it IMPROVES learning of a specific concept, never by whether it looks impressive. Because attention, screen space and generation credits are scarce for a single INBDE/TOEFL learner, every produced asset competes with the null option of plain text and must beat it on learning outcome. This KB supplies the SCIENCE (Mayer's CTML and its principles, the 3D-vs-2D anatomy evidence, the cost-ledger rule) that turns a vague 'add a picture' impulse into a defensible produce/skip/format decision; the production pipeline and the occlusion consumer are neighboring slices this frame feeds [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the underlying learning science; scarcity/single-user context is a project FACT].

included: the scarcity of attention/screen/credits that makes text the default
this KB as the decision science feeding production and occlusion
excluded: the occlusion card lifecycle in contenteng

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: engagement evidence or a pipeline contract change revises the frame

pros.claim: Framing media as an intervention with a null (text) baseline forces every asset to justify itself and prevents decorative bloat
pros.example: declining to generate an image for the arbitrary fact 'the INBDE has 500 items' because text conveys it with zero visual cost

cons.claim: A strict outcome frame can under-produce motivating imagery that aids engagement even without direct learning gain
cons.example: skipping a friendly diagram that would have kept a fatigued learner on task

failure_modes: treating visual polish as evidence of pedagogical value
producing media by default instead of justifying it against plain text
acceptance_tests: the frame states media is judged by learning outcome, names text as the null baseline, and scopes this KB as the decision science feeding production
revisit_triggers: engagement data shows motivational value of media the outcome frame ignores
the production pipeline contract changes
the learner population widens beyond single-user

nodes.definition: State the three assumptions of Mayer's cognitive theory of multimedia learning that bound every downstream decision: (1) DUAL CHANNELS — humans process pictorial/visual material and verbal/auditory material in separate channels (Paivio dual-coding; Baddeley's visuospatial sketchpad and phonological loop); (2) LIMITED CAPACITY — each channel can hold and process only a few elements at once; (3) ACTIVE PROCESSING — meaningful learning requires the learner to select relevant material, organise it into a coherent structure, and integrate it with prior knowledge. Together these mean a visual is not free: it consumes limited visual-channel capacity, so a visual that does not repay that capacity with organised, integrable information is a net loss [ESTIMATE — to source-verify; this is the canonical CTML statement but not re-derived from primary sources here].

excluded: the specific load taxonomy (its own node)
the design principles derived from these assumptions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fetching primary CTML sources or expertise-reversal evidence revises the assumptions

pros.claim: Grounding decisions in dual-channel limited capacity explains WHY every later principle works, so the principles are not arbitrary rules
pros.example: deriving 'do not add on-screen text over narration' from within-channel overload rather than memorising it

cons.claim: The assumptions are a simplified model of working memory that individual differences and rich prior knowledge can complicate
cons.example: an expert whose large schemas let them process a dense visual the limited-capacity model would predict overloads

failure_modes: treating a visual as cost-free capacity
collapsing the visual and verbal channels into one undifferentiated store
acceptance_tests: the three assumptions are named with the Paivio/Baddeley grounding and the consequence that visual capacity is finite is drawn, tagged ESTIMATE to source-verify
revisit_triggers: the primary CTML sources are fetched and a claim needs correction
expertise-reversal evidence contradicts a capacity prediction
a channel-count refinement is adopted

nodes.definition: Fix the cognitive-load taxonomy that the media producer manipulates. INTRINSIC (essential) load is set by the content's inherent complexity and element interactivity — the number of interacting parts that must be held together (a single term = low; the branching of the trigeminal nerve = high) and is not reducible by design, only by segmenting/pretraining. EXTRANEOUS (incidental) load is imposed by the PRESENTATION — split attention, seductive detail, redundant text — and is pure waste the producer must minimise. GERMANE (generative) load is the desirable effort of building and automating a schema, which freed capacity should go toward. The producer's lever is almost entirely extraneous-load reduction: make the visual carry essential structure with the least incidental burden [ESTIMATE — to source-verify; Sweller's cognitive load theory as commonly stated].

included: extraneous load from presentation as the producer's lever
germane load as the desired destination of freed capacity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a refined load taxonomy or a load-measurement method changes the lever

pros.claim: Separating intrinsic from extraneous load tells the producer what design can fix (extraneous) versus what only content restructuring can fix (intrinsic)
pros.example: recognising that a cluttered nerve diagram's problem is extraneous clutter, fixable by design, not the nerve's inherent complexity

cons.claim: The three loads are hard to measure separately and the germane category has been contested and refined in the literature
cons.example: being unable to say numerically how much of a struggling learner's load is extraneous versus intrinsic

failure_modes: blaming content complexity for what is actually extraneous design load
adding visual richness in the name of germane load when it is really extraneous
acceptance_tests: the three load types are defined, intrinsic is tied to element interactivity, extraneous is identified as the producer's lever, and germane as the freed-capacity destination
revisit_triggers: a refined load taxonomy is adopted
a measurement method for the loads becomes available
germane load's status is revised in a fetched source

nodes.definition: Recast the load taxonomy in Mayer's instructional-goal terms, because the design principles are organised by which demand they target. EXTRANEOUS processing is cognitive effort wasted on poorly designed presentation and is reduced by the coherence, signaling, redundancy, spatial-contiguity and temporal-contiguity principles. ESSENTIAL processing is the effort needed to mentally represent inherently complex material and is managed by segmenting, pretraining and modality. GENERATIVE processing is deep sense-making the learner should be motivated toward once the other two are handled. This mapping is the producer's checklist: first strip extraneous, then help manage essential, so freed capacity is available for generative learning [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

included: which principle families target each goal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a re-classification of a principle across demands changes the mapping

pros.claim: Organising principles by the demand they target gives a producer an ordered checklist instead of an unstructured list of rules
pros.example: knowing to first remove seductive detail (extraneous) before deciding whether to segment a complex model (essential)

cons.claim: A principle can affect more than one demand, so the neat mapping is an approximation
cons.example: signaling reducing extraneous search while also supporting essential organisation, blurring the category

failure_modes: applying an essential-management principle before extraneous load is removed
treating the demand categories as strictly exclusive
acceptance_tests: the three processing demands are mapped to their principle families and the strip-then-manage-then-motivate ordering is stated
revisit_triggers: a principle is re-classified across demands
the primary source refines the mapping
a new principle must be placed

nodes.definition: State the base principle and its condition: people learn better from words AND pictures than from words alone — the empirical warrant for producing card media at all — BUT the effect holds only when the picture is RELEVANT to the content and DESIGNED to support the other principles; an irrelevant or decorative picture reverses into a coherence violation. So the multimedia principle does NOT license adding an image to every card; it licenses adding a relevant, structure-carrying image where one exists. For verbal or arbitrary facts (a definition, a date, a rule number) there is no picture that carries information words cannot, and the principle offers no benefit to capture [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. This is the single most-abused principle: read as 'always add a picture' it produces exactly the decorative bloat the coherence principle forbids.

included: the relevance/design condition on the benefit
the no-benefit case for verbal/arbitrary facts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a formalised relevance heuristic or observed decorative leakage revises the condition

pros.claim: Stating the condition alongside the principle blocks the 'always add a picture' misreading at the source
pros.example: producing a diagram for tooth-surface orientation but not for the definition of 'caries', because only the former has structure a picture carries

cons.claim: The boundary between a relevant and a merely decorative picture is a judgement call that can be gamed to justify almost any image
cons.example: rationalising a generic mouth photo on a pharmacology card as 'relevant context'

failure_modes: reading the principle as 'always add a picture'
adding a topically-adjacent but non-informative image and calling it relevant
acceptance_tests: the principle is stated with its relevance/design condition and the explicit no-benefit case for verbal/arbitrary facts
revisit_triggers: a relevance heuristic is formalised
a fetched source sharpens the boundary condition
decorative images slip past the relevance test in practice

nodes.definition: State the coherence principle: learning improves when extraneous words, sounds, and images are EXCLUDED. The subordinate seductive-details effect is the specific, well-replicated harm of adding interesting-but-irrelevant material (a dramatic photo, a fun fact, background music) that attracts attention, competes for limited capacity, and disrupts the learner's schema building — it can lower learning even though learners rate it as more enjoyable [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. For a produced anatomy diagram this means: no ornamental shading, no unrelated background, no extra structures beyond the one the card tests. Coherence is the direct operational counterweight to a naive reading of the multimedia principle, and the primary reason the house rule defaults to LESS media, not more.

included: the seductive-details effect and its enjoyment-vs-learning gap
excluded: the antipattern catalogue for card media (its own node)
the signaling of what to keep

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a documented orientation exception or a refined seductive-details boundary changes the exclusion rule

pros.claim: Coherence gives a concrete subtractive rule that reliably improves a visual by removing rather than adding
pros.example: stripping a generated diagram's decorative gradient and unrelated adjacent teeth so only the tested structure remains

cons.claim: Aggressive exclusion can remove orienting context a novice needs to locate the structure
cons.example: cropping a nerve so tightly the learner cannot tell which side of the jaw it is on

failure_modes: adding seductive detail to raise perceived quality
over-stripping context a novice needs for orientation
acceptance_tests: coherence-as-exclusion is stated, the seductive-details effect with its enjoyment-vs-learning gap is named, and the default-to-leaner-media consequence is drawn
revisit_triggers: a novice-orientation exception is documented
the seductive-details boundary is refined by a fetched source
learners report disorientation from over-stripped visuals

nodes.definition: State the signaling (cueing) principle: adding cues that highlight the essential material or its organisation — arrows, colour highlights, bold labels, an outline, motion pointing — improves learning WITHOUT adding new content, by directing the learner's limited attention to what matters and away from searching. Unlike the multimedia principle, signaling adds no information cost; it only reduces extraneous search load, so it is nearly always safe to apply on a produced diagram. For card media this is the lever that turns a busy anatomical image into a legible one: the single structure the card tests is cued, its label is emphasised, and competing detail is de-emphasised rather than deleted [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. Signaling and coherence are complementary: coherence removes the irrelevant, signaling foregrounds the relevant.

included: cues that highlight essential material or organisation
excluded: the spatial placement of labels (contiguity node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a signaling-density guideline or eye-tracking evidence changes the cueing rule

pros.claim: Signaling improves comprehension at almost no risk because it adds guidance not content
pros.example: an arrow and a bold label pointing to the mental foramen so the eye lands there before reading

cons.claim: Over-signaling (too many arrows, too much highlight) becomes visual noise that re-imposes extraneous load
cons.example: a diagram where every structure is arrowed so no single cue stands out

failure_modes: leaving the tested structure un-cued in a busy image
over-cueing until the cues themselves are clutter
acceptance_tests: signaling is stated as zero-content attention cueing that reduces extraneous search, with the over-signaling failure noted
revisit_triggers: a signaling-density guideline is set
eye-tracking shows cues are missed or ignored
a new cue type is introduced

nodes.definition: State the redundancy principle: presenting a graphic with spoken narration usually produces better learning than the SAME graphic with narration PLUS identical on-screen text, because the printed and spoken words are redundant and the printed words force the visual channel to split between reading and viewing the graphic. The effect is strongest when the material is transient and fast-paced; it weakens or reverses when text is the only verbal source, when words are technical/unfamiliar, or for non-native speakers who benefit from seeing the words [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. For a mostly-static flashcard the redundancy risk is lower than for animation, but the lesson still holds: do not duplicate a caption both as on-image text and as the card's prompt text where it splits attention without adding meaning.

included: the within-visual-channel split as the mechanism
excluded: the modality principle's narration-over-text claim (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: adding narration or a TOEFL label-need conflict changes the redundancy call

pros.claim: Redundancy warns against the intuitive but harmful habit of captioning everything that is also spoken or prompted
pros.example: not baking the full answer text into a diagram that the card already shows as the prompt

cons.claim: The exceptions (non-native learners, unfamiliar terms, static self-paced cards) are exactly this app's TOEFL and INBDE context, so the principle applies weakly and must not be over-generalised
cons.example: removing a term label a TOEFL learner actually needs to see spelled out

failure_modes: duplicating spoken/prompt text as on-image text that splits attention
over-applying the principle and stripping labels non-native or novice learners need
acceptance_tests: the redundancy principle and its within-channel-split mechanism are stated with the transient/technical/non-native exceptions that qualify it for this app
revisit_triggers: voice/narration is added to cards raising redundancy risk
TOEFL-learner label needs contradict the principle
a fetched source sharpens the exceptions

nodes.definition: State the spatial contiguity principle: corresponding words and pictures should be placed NEAR each other rather than far apart on the page/screen, because separated labels force the learner to hold a term in memory while visually searching for its referent (the split-attention effect), wasting limited capacity. For a produced anatomical diagram this is directly operational: place each label adjacent to the structure it names with a short leader line, rather than numbering structures and listing names in a distant legend. Legends and keys are the canonical split-attention antipattern this principle forbids for learning material (as opposed to reference material) [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. It is one of the highest-leverage, lowest-cost layout rules for card imagery.

included: placing corresponding words and pictures near each other
adjacent labels vs distant legends for learning material

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a label-collision rule or a reveal-interaction need changes the placement rule

pros.claim: Adjacent labelling removes split-attention search at essentially zero cost and is trivially checkable in a produced image
pros.example: labelling the periodontal ligament right beside it instead of as '#4' keyed to a side list

cons.claim: Dense structures may have no room for adjacent labels without overlap, forcing leader lines or a reveal interaction
cons.example: a crowded root-canal cross-section where adjacent labels would collide

failure_modes: using a numbered legend for learning material
packing so many adjacent labels they overlap and re-impose search
acceptance_tests: spatial contiguity is stated with the split-attention mechanism and the adjacent-label-not-distant-legend rule for learning material
revisit_triggers: a dense structure needs a reveal interaction instead of static labels
a label-collision layout rule is set
the reference-vs-learning distinction is revisited

nodes.definition: State the temporal contiguity principle: corresponding words and pictures should be presented at the SAME time rather than successively, so the learner can build referential connections in working memory without having to hold one representation while waiting for the other. It is the time-domain twin of spatial contiguity and matters mainly for narrated animation and multi-step reveals; for a static flashcard it mostly reduces to 'show the label with the image, not on a later tap' [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. For the 3D pipeline and any segmented/animated reveal it becomes load-bearing: a rotation narrated out of sync with what is on screen forces the learner to reconcile mismatched streams, so narration and view state must be synchronised.

included: simultaneous presentation of corresponding words and pictures
its salience for animation/narration and multi-step reveals
sync of narration with 3D view state

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: producing narrated animation or a delayed reveal raises the principle's weight

pros.claim: Temporal contiguity prevents the reconcile-mismatched-streams cost in any narrated or animated 3D presentation
pros.example: narrating 'the mandibular canal runs here' exactly as the model rotates to show it, not before or after

cons.claim: For a purely static card the principle is nearly vacuous, so over-emphasising it wastes design attention
cons.example: belabouring simultaneity on a still image where word and picture are already co-present

failure_modes: desynchronising narration from a 3D rotation or animated reveal
gating a label behind a later interaction that separates it in time from the image
acceptance_tests: temporal contiguity is stated as same-time presentation, its salience for animation/narration is identified, and the narration-view-sync requirement for 3D is drawn
revisit_triggers: narrated animation or 3D flythrough is produced
a delayed-reveal interaction is added
sync tolerances need specifying

nodes.definition: State the modality principle: for a transient graphic or animation, presenting the accompanying words as SPOKEN narration can beat presenting them as on-screen text, because narration uses the auditory/verbal channel and leaves the visual channel free for the graphic, whereas on-screen text competes with the graphic for the same visual channel. It is the constructive complement of redundancy: redundancy says do not put spoken and printed words together; modality says when a graphic is transient, prefer the spoken form. Boundaries: it weakens for self-paced static material, for technical terms whose spelling matters, and for non-native learners — again this app's TOEFL/INBDE case — so for silent static flashcards on-image text is often the right choice and modality applies mainly if narrated 3D flythroughs are produced [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

included: narration freeing the visual channel for a transient graphic
modality as the complement of redundancy
the self-paced/technical/non-native boundaries for this app

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: producing narrated media or adding card audio raises the principle's relevance

pros.claim: Modality tells the producer WHEN to prefer audio over text, completing the redundancy guidance rather than contradicting it
pros.example: narrating a 3D mandible flythrough instead of overlaying text that would occlude the model

cons.claim: Its boundary conditions (technical terms, non-native, self-paced) dominate this app's context, so it rarely fires for static cards and can mislead if applied by default
cons.example: narrating a term a TOEFL learner needs to see spelled and losing the orthographic learning

failure_modes: applying modality to self-paced static cards where text is better
narrating spellings-critical terms non-native learners must read
acceptance_tests: modality is stated as narration-frees-visual-channel for transient graphics, positioned as redundancy's complement, with the boundaries that make it rare for this app's static cards
revisit_triggers: narrated 3D or animated media is produced
the app adds audio to cards
boundary evidence for non-native learners is refined

nodes.definition: State the two essential-processing management principles. SEGMENTING: break a complex presentation into learner-paced parts (a step-through, a layered reveal) so intrinsic load arrives in digestible chunks rather than all at once. PRETRAINING: teach the names, locations and characteristics of the key components BEFORE the full integrated presentation, so working memory is not simultaneously learning the parts and how they interact. Both attack intrinsic/essential load, which coherence and signaling cannot reduce because it is inherent to the content [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. For a complex head-and-neck structure this means: name the parts first, then reveal the relations one layer at a time, rather than dropping a fully-labelled dense 3D model on a novice — the direct instructional-design rationale for staged reveals and for pretraining vocabulary in a prerequisite card.

included: attacking intrinsic load design cannot otherwise reduce

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an overload without segmenting or a reveal-cost measurement changes the essential-load policy

pros.claim: Segmenting and pretraining are the only levers for inherently complex structures, letting rich anatomy be taught without overload
pros.example: a prerequisite card teaching the names of the mandibular nerve branches before a card testing their spatial relations

cons.claim: Both add production and scheduling overhead (extra reveal states or prerequisite cards) that is wasted on simple content
cons.example: building a staged reveal for a two-part structure a single labelled image would teach

failure_modes: dropping a fully-labelled dense model on a novice with no pretraining
segmenting trivial content and adding needless interaction steps
acceptance_tests: segmenting and pretraining are defined as essential-load management, distinguished from the extraneous-load principles, and mapped to staged reveals and prerequisite vocabulary cards
revisit_triggers: a complex structure overloads learners without segmenting
the prerequisite-card mechanism changes in contenteng
reveal-state cost is measured

nodes.definition: Establish that the benefit of a rich visual, especially 3D, is MODERATED by the learner's visuospatial ability, not constant. Two competing hypotheses recur in the anatomy-education literature: the ABILITY-AS-COMPENSATOR view, where a fully rendered external 3D model does the spatial work for low-spatial learners and helps them most; and the ABILITY-AS-ENHANCER / expertise-reversal view, where added visual richness benefits high-ability or advanced learners who can exploit it while OVERLOADING or under-serving others for whom a clean 2D image suffices [ESTIMATE — to source-verify; both hypotheses are reported with mixed support]. The single-user consequence: 3D is not universally better, its value depends on THIS learner's spatial ability and expertise, and without that measurement the safe prior is that 3D helps only genuinely volumetric content and can otherwise waste capacity.

the single-user safe prior without ability data
excluded: the aggregate 3D-vs-2D outcome evidence (its own node)

cons.claim: This app does not measure the learner's spatial ability, so the moderator is known to matter but cannot be applied precisely, only as a cautious prior
cons.example: having to default conservatively because no visuospatial score exists for the single user

failure_modes: assuming 3D benefit is constant across learners
claiming to tune to spatial ability the app never measures

nodes.definition: State the anatomy-education evidence on 3D versus 2D honestly: results are MIXED and content-dependent, not a clean win for 3D. The consistent signal is that interactive/stereoscopic 3D helps most for learning INHERENTLY SPATIAL structural relations — how parts occupy and relate in volume (the course of a nerve through bone, the 3D arrangement of root canals) — where a 2D projection genuinely loses information; for content that is essentially 2D, verbal, or list-like, 3D adds cost without payoff and can distract [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. Meta-analytic and trial results diverge because studies differ in guidance, learner ability (see the moderator), and outcome type (identification vs spatial reasoning). The honest posture: 3D is a targeted tool for volumetric spatial relations, not a general upgrade, and its edge over a good labelled 2D image is narrow and conditional.

included: 3D's edge concentrated on inherently volumetric spatial relations
why study results diverge (guidance, ability, outcome type)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: source-verifying a meta-analysis or collecting 3D-card outcomes changes the evidence posture

pros.claim: An honest mixed-evidence statement stops 3D from being sold as a universal upgrade and pins its benefit to volumetric content
pros.example: recommending 3D for the spatial course of the inferior alveolar nerve but a labelled 2D image for a tooth-numbering chart

cons.claim: Without this app's own outcome data the boundary of 'inherently spatial enough for 3D' remains a judgement that can be drawn too generously
cons.example: classifying a mostly-2D surface anatomy as volumetric to justify a 3D model

nodes.definition: Analyse the two things 3D actually adds and their two-sided cost. STEREOPSIS/DEPTH cues and free ROTATION let a learner recover volumetric structure a static 2D projection hides, which is the genuine mechanism behind 3D's benefit for spatial relations. But the MANIPULATION itself imposes extraneous load: deciding how to rotate, losing orientation, and managing the interface all consume capacity that is not learning the anatomy, and studies find unguided free exploration can equal or underperform a well-chosen set of static views [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. The design consequence: prefer a small number of instructor-chosen key viewpoints (or a guided rotation path) over dumping a free-orbit model on the learner, and reserve full free manipulation for when the learning objective IS spatial manipulation itself.

included: stereopsis/rotation as the real 3D benefit mechanism
preferring key viewpoints/guided paths over free orbit
excluded: the guidance/fading instructional support detail (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: free-orbit underperformance or a manipulation-objective card changes the interactivity rule

pros.claim: Separating the benefit (depth/rotation) from the cost (manipulation load) yields the concrete rule to constrain viewpoints
pros.example: shipping three labelled key views of a mandible with an optional guided rotate rather than a raw free-orbit model

cons.claim: Constraining viewpoints removes the exploratory agency that motivates some learners and can help genuine spatial-manipulation objectives
cons.example: limiting rotation on a card whose whole point is rotating the structure to find a hidden foramen

failure_modes: shipping an unguided free-orbit model as the default
removing manipulation from a task whose objective is spatial manipulation

nodes.definition: Establish that 3D only pays off WITH instructional support, and that support should fade with expertise. A raw model — even of genuinely volumetric anatomy — leaves a novice not knowing where to look or what relation matters, so signaling (labels, highlighted target structures, a narrated or captioned focus) must accompany it, and complex models should be segmented and pretrained. As the learner gains expertise the guidance should FADE (the guidance-fading effect), because scaffolding that helps a novice becomes redundant and mildly harmful for an expert (an expertise-reversal within the same learner over time) [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. This unifies the signaling, segmenting/pretraining and spatial-ability threads onto the 3D case: a produced 3D asset ships with cueing and staged reveal by default, relaxing as mastery rises.

included: 3D requiring signaling/segmenting support to pay off
excluded: the raw stereopsis/rotation mechanism (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a fading mastery signal or an over-scaffolding harm changes the guidance policy

pros.claim: Requiring guidance-by-default and fading prevents both the unguided-novice-overload and the over-scaffolded-expert failures
pros.example: a first-encounter 3D nerve card with labels and a highlighted path, later reduced to an unlabelled model as mastery grows

cons.claim: Fading needs a mastery signal to time it, coupling this to the learner model and adding a dependency the media producer does not own
cons.example: not knowing when to remove labels without a mastery estimate from the learner specialist

failure_modes: shipping an unguided 3D model to a novice
keeping full scaffolding on for an expert (expertise reversal)
acceptance_tests: 3D-needs-guidance and guidance-fading-with-expertise are stated, and the reliance on a mastery signal to time fading is acknowledged
revisit_triggers: a mastery signal for fading becomes available from the learner model

nodes.definition: Define the cost side of the earns-its-cost decision as an explicit ledger. A produced visual costs on three axes: PRODUCTION (generation credits/time for an image via the Codex MCP generator or a 3D asset via Tripo, plus authoring/QA effort), REAL ESTATE (screen space and the learner's time to parse it), and PROCESSING LOAD (the extraneous capacity it consumes even when well-designed, which is never zero). Against this sits the PAYOFF: learning the visual enables that words alone cannot deliver — which per the multimedia principle and the 3D evidence exists only when the content carries spatial/structural information. The ledger makes the decision quantitative-in-spirit: a visual is justified only when payoff outweighs the summed cost, and for verbal/arbitrary facts payoff is ~zero so any cost loses [ESTIMATE for the load axis; production/credit cost is a project FACT that generation consumes budget].

excluded: the produce/skip rule itself (its own node)
the exact credit pricing (UNKNOWN per EXTERNAL_RECON)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: obtaining credit pricing or a load proxy sharpens the ledger

pros.claim: An explicit ledger converts a gut 'should I add a picture' into a defensible cost-vs-payoff comparison
pros.example: rejecting a generated image for a rote drug name because production and load cost buy no words-cannot-convey payoff

cons.claim: The payoff and processing-load terms are not directly measured, so the ledger is a reasoning frame not a computed number
cons.example: having to estimate a diagram's extraneous load qualitatively rather than measuring it

failure_modes: ignoring the always-nonzero processing-load cost and treating well-designed media as free
counting production credits but not the learner's parsing time
acceptance_tests: the three cost axes and the words-cannot-convey payoff are stated, and the payoff-outweighs-summed-cost rule with the ~zero-payoff verbal-fact case is drawn
revisit_triggers: actual Tripo/Codex credit pricing is obtained
a processing-load proxy becomes measurable
the payoff can be validated against learner outcomes

nodes.definition: State the central decision rule this KB exists to supply. A diagram or 3D model EARNS its cognitive cost only when BOTH hold: (1) the content is inherently SPATIAL or STRUCTURAL — the learning objective involves how things are arranged, connected, or shaped in space — so a picture carries information words cannot; and (2) the visual is designed to the principles (coherent, signaled, contiguous) so its extraneous load is minimised. When content is verbal, arbitrary, or list-like (definitions, rules, dates, drug names), no picture carries information words cannot, payoff is ~zero, and the visual is DECORATION that the coherence principle actively forbids — default to text. This rule is the operational synthesis of the multimedia principle (conditional benefit), coherence (exclude the extraneous), the 3D evidence (volumetric content only), and the cost ledger (payoff must beat cost); it is deliberately biased toward SKIP because the failure mode of media production is over-production [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the science; the skip-bias is a defensible house judgement].

included: the two-part earns-its-cost test (inherently spatial AND well-designed)
excluded: the format choice between 2D and 3D (production gate)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a spatial-content classifier or outcome calibration data changes the rule's threshold

pros.claim: A single testable rule collapses four principles into one produce/skip gate a producer can apply per card
pros.example: asking 'is this content inherently spatial and can I design it cleanly?' and skipping media whenever the answer is no

cons.claim: The 'inherently spatial' test is a judgement that can be stretched, and a strict skip-bias may under-serve borderline spatial content that a picture would modestly help
cons.example: skipping a mild spatial-mnemonic image that would have helped a struggling learner

failure_modes: producing media for verbal/arbitrary facts (decoration)
stretching 'inherently spatial' to justify a picture on anything
acceptance_tests: the two-part rule (inherently spatial AND well-designed) is stated, the default-to-text for verbal content is drawn, and the skip-bias against over-production is made explicit
revisit_triggers: borderline spatial content is chronically under- or over-served
a relevance/spatial classifier is built
learner-outcome data lets the rule be calibrated

nodes.definition: Catalogue the concrete decoration antipatterns the earns-its-cost rule and coherence principle forbid, so the producer can recognise them fast: (1) the SEDUCTIVE stock image — a mouth photo on a pharmacology card, an ornamental icon — topically adjacent but carrying no tested structure; (2) the DECORATIVE 3D model — a rotating tooth on a card that tests a fact, not a spatial relation, all cost and no payoff; (3) the LEGEND-KEYED diagram violating spatial contiguity; (4) the OVER-SIGNALED image where every part is arrowed; (5) the REDUNDANT caption duplicating the prompt text into the image; (6) the UNGUIDED free-orbit model dropped on a novice. Each is a specific failure of a named principle, and each has the same fix: remove it or redesign it to carry tested structure. This node turns the abstract rule into a fast recognisable checklist for review [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the underlying effects; the catalogue is design synthesis].

excluded: the positive occlusion-image spec (its own node)

cons.claim: A pattern list can be applied mechanically and miss a case that is technically decorative but genuinely motivating
cons.example: reflexively cutting a light illustrative image that was keeping a fatigued learner engaged

failure_modes: shipping any catalogued antipattern unrecognised
mechanically cutting a borderline image without weighing engagement
acceptance_tests: the antipatterns are listed with the principle each violates and the shared remove-or-redesign fix, usable as a review checklist
revisit_triggers: a new antipattern recurs in produced media

nodes.definition: Emit the pedagogical spec for a produced image-occlusion diagram that contenteng consumes (contenteng owns the occlusion CARD; this KB owns the IMAGE's pedagogy). Requirements: (1) SIGNALING — the structure under each occludable region is visually clear and unambiguous so a masked region is a well-defined retrieval target; (2) SPATIAL CONTIGUITY — each label sits adjacent to its referent, never in a distant legend, because occlusion cards hide labels and a distant key breaks the mask semantics; (3) COHERENCE — no seductive background or extra structures that could be accidentally occluded into ambiguity; (4) ONE-TESTABLE-STRUCTURE-PER-REGION — each occludable region isolates a single retrievable fact so grading is unambiguous; (5) sufficient RESOLUTION and contrast for the region to be readable when the rest is masked. This is the positive counterpart to the antipattern catalogue and the contract handed to the occlusion consumer [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the principles; the occlusion-consumer boundary is a project FACT per SPECIALIST_LIST].

included: signaling, spatial contiguity, coherence applied to occlusion images

excluded: the occlusion card object model and mask editing (contenteng)

nodes.definition: Define the gate that decides whether to invoke the image->Tripo->GLB-><model-viewer> 3D pipeline instead of producing a 2D image. Invoke 3D only when ALL hold: (1) the content is inherently VOLUMETRIC — the objective is a spatial relation a 2D projection genuinely loses (per the 3D-vs-2D evidence); (2) the model can be shipped with GUIDANCE — signaling, constrained key viewpoints or a guided path, and segmenting/pretraining for complexity (per the interactivity and guidance nodes); (3) the cost is JUSTIFIED on the ledger given Tripo generation credits and the extraneous manipulation load. Otherwise default to a signaled 2D image. The downstream mechanics are a neighboring slice: Tripo emits a GLB (model.glb / pbr_model) that Google's <model-viewer> web component renders in-browser via a three.js loader [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]; exact Tripo pricing is [UNKNOWN — METHOD: platform.tripo3d.ai/docs/billing]. This gate is the format-selection layer of the media verdict.

nodes.definition: Compose the produce/skip/format verdict the KB builds toward, applied per card+concept. SKIP media (default) when the content is verbal, arbitrary, or list-like — text wins on the cost ledger. Produce a SIGNALED 2D IMAGE when the content is spatial-on-a-plane or structural-but-flat (a labelled diagram, an occlusion image to the IMAGE_OCCLUSION_MEDIA_SPEC) — applying coherence, signaling and spatial/temporal contiguity. Invoke the GATED 3D pipeline only when the THREED_PRODUCTION_GATE's volumetric-AND-guided-AND-cost-justified test passes, shipping the GLB with signaling and constrained viewpoints. Across all branches: minimise extraneous load, exclude decoration, and when two formats are close on payoff choose the CHEAPER, more honest one. The verdict is deliberately skip-biased because over-production is the dominant failure mode of a media generator, and every produced asset must trace its justification to an inherently spatial/structural payoff [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the science; the policy is design synthesis grounded in the earlier nodes].

excluded: the production pipeline mechanics and generator prompts
the occlusion card and 3D viewer implementation

failure_modes: defaulting to produce instead of skip

acceptance_tests: the verdict states the three-branch skip/2D/gated-3D policy, the minimise-extraneous and cheaper-on-tie rules, and the skip-bias with a traceable spatial/structural justification per asset

edges.why_related: the media-as-intervention frame is grounded in the dual-channel limited-capacity model of why visuals cost capacity
limited per-channel capacity is what the intrinsic/extraneous/germane load taxonomy partitions
Mayer's essential/incidental/generative processing recasts the load taxonomy in instructional-goal terms
words-plus-pictures works because the two channels can carry complementary representations
coherence targets the extraneous-processing demand by excluding irrelevant material
signaling targets extraneous processing by cueing attention to essential material
redundancy harm arises from duplicated words overloading the visual channel
spatial contiguity reduces the extraneous split-attention load of separated words and pictures
temporal contiguity reduces extraneous load by presenting corresponding words and pictures at the same time
modality is the constructive complement of redundancy, prescribing narration where redundancy forbids duplication
segmenting and pretraining manage the intrinsic/essential load the load taxonomy defines
spatial ability moderates how much of the limited visual channel a learner can exploit for 3D
the 3D-vs-2D question is a special case of the conditional words-plus-pictures benefit for volumetric content
the mixed 3D-vs-2D evidence is partly explained by the spatial-ability moderator
interactivity and stereopsis are the mechanisms behind whatever 3D-over-2D benefit exists
the manipulation cost of interactive 3D is an instance of extraneous load
3D pays off only with instructional guidance, so the guidance/fading rule extends the 3D-vs-2D finding
the processing-load axis of the cost ledger is the extraneous load from the load taxonomy
the earns-its-cost rule is the payoff-outweighs-cost verdict computed on the ledger
the rule's inherently-spatial condition is grounded in the 3D-vs-2D evidence about when visuals carry unique information
the rule operationalises the multimedia principle's conditional benefit into a produce/skip test
the antipatterns are concrete violations of the coherence principle
the antipattern catalogue enumerates media that fails the earns-its-cost rule
the occlusion spec requires adjacent labels, a direct application of spatial contiguity
the occlusion spec applies only to images that have passed the earns-its-cost rule
the 3D gate is the format branch taken after the earns-its-cost rule says produce a visual
the gate's guided-viewpoints requirement follows from the manipulation-cost analysis
the gate requires shipping guidance, which the guidance/fading node specifies
the verdict's branches all derive from the earns-its-cost produce/skip decision
the 2D branch of the verdict emits the occlusion/diagram spec
the gated-3D branch of the verdict is the production gate's output
the verdict's exclude-decoration rule enforces the antipattern catalogue
the multimedia principle pulls toward adding pictures while coherence pulls toward excluding all but the essential, and a naive read of the former produces exactly what the latter forbids
edges.resolution_rule: coherence wins by default: add a picture only when it carries inherently spatial/structural information words cannot, otherwise exclude it; the multimedia benefit is conditional, coherence is the safeguard

edges.why_related: 3D's richer spatial payoff tempts production while the cost ledger counts its generation credits and manipulation load against it
edges.resolution_rule: invoke 3D only when the volumetric payoff clears the summed ledger cost; for non-volumetric content the ledger wins and a 2D image or text is chosen

edges.why_related: applying signaling to a diagram causally makes each occludable region an unambiguous retrieval target in the spec
coherence violations causally raise the processing-load cost term in the ledger
segmenting/pretraining and 3D guidance are the same essential-load management applied to static and 3D media respectively
misroutes surfaced by applying the verdict feed back to recalibrate the earns-its-cost threshold

conflict_axes.name: richness_vs_cognitive_load

workflow.gate: coherence, signaling, spatial and temporal contiguity, and redundancy/modality are applied with their boundary exceptions

workflow.action: Manage essential load for complex structures
workflow.description: Segment complex presentations and pretrain component names before integration
workflow.gate: segmenting and pretraining are specified for content whose intrinsic load is high

workflow.action: Assess the 3D-vs-2D evidence and its moderators
workflow.description: State that 3D helps mainly inherently volumetric relations, moderated by spatial ability and guidance
workflow.gate: the mixed content-dependent evidence, the spatial-ability moderator, and the volumetric-content boundary are stated, tagged ESTIMATE

workflow.action: Analyse interactivity cost and required guidance
workflow.description: Separate stereopsis/rotation benefit from manipulation cost and require guided viewpoints with fading
workflow.gate: the benefit mechanism, the manipulation-load cost, and the guided-viewpoints-with-fading rule are stated

workflow.action: Build the cost ledger and earns-its-cost rule
workflow.description: Sum production/real-estate/processing costs against words-cannot-convey payoff and require inherently spatial content
workflow.gate: the cost ledger and the two-part rule with the default-to-text skip-bias are stated
the antipatterns are listed with the principle each violates and the remove-or-redesign fix

workflow.description: Signaling, adjacent labels, coherence, one-structure-per-region, readable resolution as the contract to contenteng
workflow.gate: the spec requirements are stated and framed as the contract handed to contenteng

workflow.description: Invoke image->Tripo->GLB->model-viewer only when volumetric AND guided AND cost-justified; else 2D
workflow.gate: the three-part gate is stated, GLB/model-viewer cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7, Tripo pricing marked UNKNOWN, and the 2D default drawn

workflow.description: Route each card to skip, 2D-signaled, or gated-3D, minimising extraneous load and choosing cheaper on ties
workflow.gate: the three-branch verdict, the minimise-extraneous and cheaper-on-tie rules, and the skip-bias with traceable justification are stated

priority_rationale: The media-as-intervention frame and the CTML/load foundations come first because they decide, for every downstream choice, whether a visual repays its capacity cost; the multimedia principle and the extraneous-load principles (coherence, signaling, spatial/temporal contiguity, redundancy/modality) plus the essential-load principles (segmenting/pretraining) come next as the design vocabulary; the 3D-vs-2D evidence, its spatial-ability moderator, the interactivity cost and the guidance/fading rule form the anatomy-specific layer; and the cost ledger, earns-its-cost rule, antipattern catalogue, occlusion spec, 3D production gate and media verdict come last because they compose every principle into an auditable, skip-biased produce/skip/format decision with vendor pipeline facts traced to EXTERNAL_RECON.

dominance_rules.rule: Coherence dominates a naive reading of the multimedia principle
dominance_rules.rationale: adding a picture helps only when it carries essential structure, otherwise it is extraneous load the coherence principle forbids
dominance_rules.trigger: a picture is proposed for a card
dominance_rules.action: produce it only if it carries inherently spatial/structural information words cannot; otherwise exclude it

dominance_rules.rule: Text dominates media for verbal, arbitrary, or list-like content
dominance_rules.rationale: such content has ~zero words-cannot-convey payoff so any visual cost is a net loss
dominance_rules.trigger: the card content is a definition, rule, date, or name
dominance_rules.action: skip media and present as text

dominance_rules.rule: A signaled 2D image dominates 3D unless content is inherently volumetric
dominance_rules.rationale: 3D's edge over a good labelled 2D image is narrow and conditional on volumetric spatial relations
dominance_rules.action: require a concrete spatial relation a 2D projection loses; otherwise use a signaled 2D image

dominance_rules.rule: Guided key viewpoints dominate free-orbit exploration by default
dominance_rules.rationale: unguided manipulation imposes extraneous load and can underperform curated views
dominance_rules.action: constrain to guided viewpoints with signaling unless the objective is spatial manipulation itself

dominance_rules.rule: The skip-bias dominates the produce-bias on a borderline card
dominance_rules.rationale: over-production (decoration) is the dominant failure mode of a media generator
dominance_rules.trigger: a card's need for media is borderline
dominance_rules.action: skip unless a spatial/structural payoff is concretely traceable

dominance_rules.rule: Adjacent labels dominate legends for learning material
dominance_rules.rationale: distant legends impose split-attention load and break occlusion mask semantics
dominance_rules.trigger: a diagram or occlusion image is labelled
dominance_rules.action: place each label adjacent to its referent, reserving legends for reference-only figures

dominance_rules.rule: The cheaper honest format dominates on a payoff tie
dominance_rules.rationale: equal learning payoff means the lower-cost option wins the ledger
dominance_rules.trigger: two formats are close on expected learning payoff
dominance_rules.action: choose the cheaper, lower-load format (text over image, 2D over 3D)

dominance_rules.rule: Faded guidance dominates full scaffolding once mastery is high
dominance_rules.rationale: scaffolding that helps a novice becomes redundant or harmful for an expert (expertise reversal)
dominance_rules.trigger: the learner's mastery estimate for the structure clears a threshold

dominance_rules.rule: The verified EXTERNAL_RECON pipeline fact dominates assumed vendor capability
dominance_rules.rationale: vendor facts must trace to EXTERNAL_RECON or be carried as UNKNOWN, never invented
dominance_rules.trigger: a claim about Tripo output or the viewer is needed
dominance_rules.action: cite EXTERNAL_RECON §7 (GLB via <model-viewer>) and mark pricing/anything unlisted as UNKNOWN with a METHOD

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the earns-its-cost rule before generating any asset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending generation credits on decoration that review then deletes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Classify content as verbal / spatial-flat / volumetric before choosing a format
anti_rework_rules.prevents: producing a 3D model for content a 2D image or text would teach, then re-doing it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design occlusion images with adjacent labels from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating a legend-keyed diagram whose masked regions are ambiguous

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ship 3D models with guidance and constrained viewpoints by default
anti_rework_rules.prevents: releasing an unguided free-orbit model that overloads novices and must be re-scaffolded

anti_rework_rules.rule: Strip seductive detail and redundant on-image text before review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a coherence/redundancy rework pass after the asset is already in cards

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pretrain component names before presenting a complex integrated structure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a novice-overload failure that forces splitting the card after the fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cite EXTERNAL_RECON for vendor facts and mark unknowns before building the pipeline
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hard-coding an invented Tripo/viewer capability that later has to be ripped out

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the spatial/structural justification with each produced asset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an un-auditable media library that cannot be pruned when the skip-bias is enforced later

iteration_protocol.trigger: the primary Mayer/CTML and cognitive-load sources are fetched and source-verified
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the ESTIMATE-tagged principle claims to FACT-source or correct them
sharpen the volumetric-content boundary and the spatial-ability moderation
replace the UNKNOWN production-cost term and re-tune the 3D gate's cost arm

iteration_protocol.trigger: learner-outcome data on produced media becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: calibrate the earns-its-cost threshold and the produce/skip verdict against measured learning gains

iteration_protocol.trigger: a mastery signal for guidance-fading becomes available from the learner model
iteration_protocol.action: wire fading of signaling/labels to the mastery estimate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a card type is chronically misrouted by the verdict
iteration_protocol.action: revise the content-classification or the branch thresholds

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new decoration antipattern recurs in produced media
iteration_protocol.action: add it to the antipattern catalogue with its principle and fix
